dimensions.assessment: Affects federal departments and agencies, foreign governments in the Western Hemisphere, industry representatives, civil society groups, and artisanal miners.
dimensions.evidence: private sector organizations, industry representatives, and civil society groups that represent communities in areas affected by illicit mining

dimensions.assessment: Directs strategic planning, international cooperation, and briefings on illicit gold trade, altering policy frameworks without immediate direct changes to individual daily lives within the U.S.
dimensions.evidence: develop a comprehensive, multi-year strategy, which shall be known as the Legal Gold and Mining Partnership Strategy

dimensions.assessment: Requires the description of existing and additional foreign assistance resources needed to fully implement the strategy, but specifies no dedicated direct spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: additional foreign assistance resources needed to fully implement the Strategy

dimensions.assessment: Amends federal money laundering provisions regarding precious metals and creates a comprehensive multi-agency international strategy.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5318A(c)(2) of title 31, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a multi-year strategy with recurring semiannual briefings required for the following three years.
dimensions.evidence: semiannually thereafter for the following 3 years

missing_information: Exact figures for additional foreign assistance funding required.
Specific staffing levels needed to execute the strategy.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a multi-year strategy to combat illicit gold mining and trafficking in the Western Hemisphere, requiring federal reporting, international coordination, and public-private partnerships. It affects federal agencies, foreign governments, mining stakeholders, and criminal networks.
